reading.body:
AI governance failure now translates into ten distinct insurance and liability exposures, several of which attach to named individuals rather than companies.

The categories pair regulatory penalties with personal accountability. Director and officer liability for AI oversight sits alongside EU AI Act conformity cover and state-level compliance exposure, so one governance failure may trigger both corporate fines and claims against executives. Workforce displacement litigation and FDA medical software non-compliance extend the same logic to labour and product risk.

Three exposures tie directly to AI's physical and compute supply chain. Greenwashing claims over data centre carbon and power usage effectiveness disclosures make energy reporting a liability issue, antitrust defence over compute allocation makes accelerator distribution a legal expense, and export control penalties attach to hardware vendors. Power and compute governance are now insurable risks, not just operational costs.

The ten categories include no dollar values, policy terms, or claim history, so they cannot show how expensive or frequent these risks are. They also do not indicate which proposals are enacted law rather than draft, including the mandatory liability insurance proposals.
